question: Of crashes in Catalonia with a death or a serious injury, the share that were fatal (someone died within 24 hours), given the recorded road, conditions and crash
source: Servei Català de Trànsit, crashes with a death or serious injury, 2010-2023
estimator: logistic regression, L2 penalty, one intercept per zone and province, effects that may differ on urban streets and on interurban roads
interval: 95% confidence interval for the share among crashes like this one: logit +- 1.96 * sqrt(x' V x), V the covariance of the coefficients over 500 bootstrap refits

levels.label: Hit an object on the road

rules.text: Tick at least one road user involved.
The number of vehicles and pedestrians must be at least the number of kinds of road user ticked.
A crash in which a pedestrian was struck must involve a pedestrian.
A collision with only one vehicle or pedestrian involved is rare in the records (73 of 22,638 crashes).
A crash involving a pedestrian and no vehicle is rare in the records (44 of 22,638 crashes).
Fewer than {threshold} recorded crashes, perhaps none, share this zone, crash type, road users and number involved: the estimate rests on the model's assumptions more than on similar crashes.
Fewer than {threshold} recorded crashes on this road have this value of {input}: the estimate for it is extrapolated, and its interval does not show how few records there are.

On roads through towns the average fatal share of such roads in the province predicted later crashes better than the model's estimates did, on 2022–2023 with the model fitted on 2010–2021, so the average is shown instead of an estimate.

evaluation.design: nested rolling origin: each year 2016-2023 predicted by a model whose penalty, specification and through-town rule were chosen, and whose coefficients were fitted, on the years before it
